hook: Bilt's killing *4%* cash back, unless you act
dek: Bilt cardholders face a deadline to opt out before losing 4% Bilt Cash rewards.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Bilt is cutting its *4% Bilt Cash* rewards for most cardholders, starting on each person's card anniversary.

slides.label: The Deadline
slides.text: You must *opt out* in the Bilt app before your anniversary date, or the switch happens automatically.

slides.label: No Going Back
slides.text: Opting out is safe, but moving to the new system is a *one-way door*, you can't switch back to 4% Bilt Cash.

slides.label: New Cardholders
slides.text: Starting in 2027, new applicants *can't choose* 4% Bilt Cash at all, that option disappears completely.

slides.label: The Upside
slides.text: *Bilt Cash now lasts 12 months* from when you earn it, instead of expiring every Dec. 31.

slides.label: The Catch
slides.text: Hotel redemptions get cut *83%*, Bilt Cash use on hotels drops from monthly to twice a year starting 2027.

slides.label: New Perk
slides.text: *Daily Rewards* launches Jan. 15, 2027, a prize program with up to $1,000,000 toward a home purchase.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: For renters and everyday spenders building credit through Bilt, missing this *deadline* could mean losing real money.

caption_instagram:
Bilt is making a huge change to its credit card rewards, and if you have a Bilt card, you need to pay attention. Thrifty Traveler reports that Bilt is killing the 4% Bilt Cash option for most cardholders, moving everyone to a new points system on your card anniversary date unless you opt out first.

Here's the catch: opting out is safe, but once you move to the new benefits, there's no going back to earning 4% back. New applicants in 2027 won't even get the choice, that option disappears completely. The good news is Bilt Cash will finally last 12 months instead of expiring every December, but hotel redemptions are getting cut hard, down 83% starting in 2027.

For people building credit and rewards through everyday spending like rent, groceries and daycare, a deadline like this can quietly cost real money if you miss it.

Opting out or letting it switch? Pick one.

caption_linkedin:
Bilt just restructured its credit card rewards program, and it's a good reminder for founders and operators building loyalty programs of your own.

Per Thrifty Traveler, Bilt is phasing out its 4% Bilt Cash option for most cardholders, moving everyone to a simplified points system on their card anniversary date unless they opt out first. The move is framed as simplification, but it comes with real tradeoffs: better expiration terms on Bilt Cash, paired with an 83% cut to hotel redemption limits starting in 2027.

The lesson for anyone running a rewards or membership program: simplifying a confusing system often means some users lose value, even when the headline sounds like an upgrade. How you communicate tradeoffs, and how much lead time you give before a deadline, matters as much as the benefit itself.

For underrepresented founders building loyalty programs, membership tiers or fintech products, this is a case study in managing change without losing member trust.
